newsitem.title: SPAIN: France, Spain to increase cooperation against ETA.
newsitem.headline: France, Spain to increase cooperation against ETA.

text.p: France pledged on Monday to increase cooperation with Spain against ETA rebels, saying it would aggressively pursue leaders of the group on its territory.
French Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre met his Spanish counterpart Jaime Mayor Oreja in Madrid to discuss joint action against the Basque guerrillas who have stepped up attacks in Spain this year.

"I have come here this evening to say to the Spanish government and to my friend Jaime the cooperation between Spain and France to fight ETA terrorism is going to increase," Debre said in an interview with state television.
"We have a community of interest. Together we can overcome terrorism in this part of the world."
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed more than 800 people in a 29-year fight for an independent Basque state encompassing parts of southern France and northern Spain.
In the past, Madrid had complained the guerrillas used the Basque region of southern France as a haven to orchestrate attacks in Spain.
But Spain's 10-month-old conservative government has repeatedly expressed its satisfaction with increasingly aggressive French action against ETA's network there.
Mayor Oreja earlier praised French authorities for a tougher stance in recent months against ETA's leadership, which he said was based in southern France.
"If the leadership of ETA is in France, it is evident we will use all means at our disposal to identify and locate it," Debre told reporters upon arrival in Spain.
In recent months, the interior ministry said France had arrested a number of important ETA activists, among them some of the group's top leaders.
"The entire leadership of ETA is in France, but not exactly intact. It is not exactly the same as it was six months ago," Mayor Oreja said in an interview published on Monday.

"The cooperation with France is exemplary. The number of detentions produced in these months, thanks to measures we have taken together with France, has been most important," he told the Spanish magazine Tribuna.

The Spanish daily El Mundo said the government was seeking to secure international support for its policies following allegations that Spanish authorities tortured a suspected ETA guerrilla arrested two weeks ago.
The government said its own investigation found that the prisoner, Fernando Elejalde, was not mistreated as Basque nationalist politicians alleged after he was caught fleeing a killing.
Spain has been criticised by international groups in the past for mistreating ETA inmates, allegations which may make neighbouring Portugal and France reluctant to extradite suspected guerrillas.

Madrid has been pressing European Union member states to ratify an extradition treaty signed in Dublin last September under which countries would no longer be able to refuse to extradite a suspect in a politically motivated crime.
Spain hopes the treaty will make it easier to prosecute ETA suspects caught abroad.
